result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers fully cover the keyboard-inaccessible div/span controls, the missing dialog semantics and focus handling, Escape and the unlabeled ×, and the failure, pending and success states. B ranks the problems by harm, says outright that the red button, consequence line and overlay look should stay, and limits its fix to the parts that change. A buries the same core points in a long list of UX, copy and CSS polish, and its sketch reorders the buttons and drops the close control, so it drifts toward a redesign. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers cover the keyboard, dialog semantics, focus, Escape and request-state problems equally well, and both suggest the native <dialog> element. A ranks fewer problems more tightly by harm and keeps the existing design with only small copy tweaks. B runs into a long tail of polish items (z-index, scroll lock, reduced motion, CSP, backdrop clicks) that buries the priorities until its closing summary.
